newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-MoDo 9 mo profit to dive 48 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-MoDo 9 mo profit to dive 48 pct.

text.p: Swedish forestry group Modo is expected to post a sharply lower profit after financial items for the first nine months of 1996 of 2.24 billion crowns, a Reuter poll of 14 analysts found on Thursday.
Forecasts varied between 1.93 billion and 2.50 billion crowns.
In the same period a year ago the company reported a profit after financial items of 4.32 billion crowns.
In the first half of 1996 the company posted a profit of 1.66 billion crowns which means analysts expected a third quarter profit of 579 million crowns.
For the full year 1996 the average forecast was for a profit after financial items of 2.70 billion crowns compared to 5.22 billion in 1995.
The average forecast for the full year was 100 million crowns lower than when Reuters last polled analysts over MoDo before the half-year report.
For 1997 analysts saw MoDo posting a profit of 2.01 billion crowns.
Analysts in August forecast next year's profit after financial items at 2.58 billion.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Carnegie, Enskilda, Fiba, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Matteus, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley, Nordbanken, Nordiska, Salomon, Swedbank and Ohman.
MoDo will release its nine month report on November 13.
